flags: MoDOT cache is map text only: no scenic-selection rationale, designation date, driving time or detailed road character. Overview does not invent these. Overview kept below 200 words because driving-character and designation evidence is thin.
Current highway history skipped the US 24 Business period (1959–1969); restored it. The cache does not quantify the bypass’s effect on traffic, so dropped “took the traffic away.”
Napoleon cache conflicts internally: namesake is qualified as most likely in History but unqualified in Geography. Preserved the qualified version.
Current cannonball remounting story rests on unnamed accounts dating from 1920. Omitted its affidavit and iron-rod details rather than turn that attributed account into an unqualified fact.
Flood susceptibility is documented; no present closure or diversion is established, so no current driving alert added.
Waterloo is short because cache evidence is thin. Its namesake sentence incorrectly says Napoleon surrendered at Waterloo; that clause is not reused.
Battle start dates and casualty figures differ among cache pages; omitted both. Battle and slavery history lack primary cached sources; editorial corroboration is desirable.
